chunks: Beasts are concerned with their bellies.
Carnivores are concerned with assaulting others.
Women are concerned with the adornments of this ignoble life and the creation of mischief herein.
ai.seo_question: What are the distinguishing characteristics of believers compared to beasts and women in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (AS) delineates the spiritual hierarchy by contrasting the instinctual drives of beasts (sustenance), carnivores (aggression), and women (worldly adornment) with the elevated state of the believers. The believers are described as *mustakinun* (humble/submissive), *mushfiqun* (vigilant/cautious), and *khaifun* (fearful of God), reflecting a state of active spiritual awareness rather than passive existence. This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on *tawadu'* (humility) and *muraqabah* (God-consciousness) as the defining traits of true faith.
